stories.title: Feather aims to build the 'Android of robotics' for developers
stories.summary: TechCrunch profiled Feather, a startup building a common software platform for robotics, similar to how Android serves phone makers. The company targets developers who build robots but lack a shared operating layer today. The report did not disclose funding or customer details.
stories.whyItMatters: A shared software layer for robotics could lower costs and speed up development across the industry, much as Android did for phones.
whatToWatch: Which robotics makers adopt Feather's platform
questions: How does Feather's approach differ from existing robotics software?

stories.title: Meta faces child safety disclosure fight as it pushes new AI products
stories.summary: The Verge reported that Meta employees were told to wear "attorney/client privilege" hats while fighting the release of child safety records, pointing to an ongoing legal battle over what Meta knew. The same day, Meta said it will let users build games with AI directly on their phones, and Ars Technica reported Meta put its AI assistant on a keychain device. Together the reports show a company launching new AI consumer products while under pressure over past child safety decisions.
stories.whyItMatters: The disclosure fight could reveal how much Meta knew about harm to children on its platforms, even as it expands AI into new hardware and app features.
whatToWatch: Whether courts force release of the internal records
Adoption of Meta's on-device AI game-building tool
Reception of the AI assistant keychain device
questions: What do the withheld records actually contain?
Will regulators respond to the disclosure fight?

stories.title: Databricks acquires Row Zero and signals more startup buys ahead
stories.summary: Databricks acquired spreadsheet startup Row Zero, according to TechCrunch, and is reportedly scouting additional startups to buy. The deal adds to Databricks' string of acquisitions as it builds out its data and AI platform. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
stories.whyItMatters: Continued acquisitions show Databricks consolidating tools around its platform, a strategy that shapes which data and AI startups stay independent.
whatToWatch: How Row Zero's product is folded into Databricks' offering
questions: What did Databricks pay for Row Zero?

stories.title: Tesla shows off the Semi truck again
stories.summary: The Verge reported another public appearance of the Tesla Semi, the electric heavy-duty truck that has faced repeated delays since its original unveiling. stories.whyItMatters: The Semi's repeated delays test Tesla's ability to deliver commercial vehicles at scale, which matters for its business beyond passenger cars.

stories.summary: The Verge reported that Microsoft is discontinuing its "Copilot Plus PC" branding, a label used for Windows laptops with dedicated AI processing hardware. The report did not specify a replacement name. The change comes as Microsoft continues pushing AI features across Windows.
stories.whyItMatters: The branding shift signals how Microsoft repositions AI-capable hardware in its messaging to PC makers and buyers.

stories.title: F-Droid ships its biggest update in a decade
stories.summary: Ars Technica reported that F-Droid, the open-source Android app store, released its largest update in ten years. The update brings a new interface and smoother app installation. F-Droid is a longtime alternative to Google Play for open-source Android apps.
stories.whyItMatters: A stronger F-Droid gives Android users a more usable option outside Google's app store, relevant to ongoing debates over app store control.
whatToWatch: User feedback on the new interface
Whether the update grows F-Droid's app catalog or install base
